Measure per request: draft latency, target verification latency, acceptance rate by position, accepted tokens per step, synchronization/barrier overhead, queue wait, time-to-first-token, end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, GPU/CPU time, memory, errors, and output-quality/equivalence checks. Record units (ms, %, tokens, tokens/s, MiB) and workload labels.

Experiment: randomize identical requests among target-only, current speculative, and draft-admission throttling arms, with matched warmup, fixed seeds/configuration, repeated trials, and a held-out trace. Sweep the intervention safely and report confidence intervals, absolute and relative effects, separating prefill/decode, cold/warm cache, prompt/output length, concurrency, and burst level.

Confounders and limits: control GPU clocks, batching/padding, cache state, allocator fragmentation, autoscaling, prompt mix, runtime versions, and telemetry overhead; inspect per-request traces rather than aggregate averages. Acceptance or speed gains do not justify output changes.

Rollback: fail closed to target-only (or the last known-good speculative setting) if output quality diverges, errors/OOMs occur, target verification is starved, memory or fairness limits are breached, or any predeclared p95/goodput SLO regresses.
